status: written after reading the complete v6.4 run and before any of the following existed: the baseline-sweep and dose-response renders, any Bonn pair, the camera height of any Argoverse 2 vehicle. H12 and H13 are registered tests; every other item is exploratory and no registered verdict depends on it. The analyses that re-use v6.4 model outputs (the cue model, the parallax check of CONVOY-REAL, the mask trade-off) had not been run on them before this amendment, but those outputs had been read.

registered_hypotheses.H12 (parallax channel: baseline sweep): BSW, 64 new base scenes with three purely parallel movers (cars and crates on the street, floating crates), each seen with the camera baseline scaled by 0.5, 1, 2 and 3: same first image, same rotation of the second camera, the mover's displacement scaled with the baseline, so s, eps = 0 and the geometric answer are unchanged and only the parallax changes. For DUSt3R and MASt3R: beta(x3) - beta(x0.5) > 0, paired cluster-bootstrap 95% CI > 0 (cluster = base scene), Holm across the two models, on movers measurable at every baseline and identifiable at x1. Rationale: in v6.4 these two models had beta_s of 0.55-0.61 for movers with more than 40 px of parallax and 0.07-0.17 below 40 px, and the other four showed no such rise; E1 cannot say whether parallax causes it. The same contrast is reported for the other models without a prediction.
registered_hypotheses.H13 (the contact junction suffices: dose: WDR, 64 new base scenes (cars and crates, purely parallel), each mover rendered without a wall and behind walls that hide at least its lowest 15, 35 and 70 cm in both views (the E5 wall, designed by ray casting; a wall must cover the whole visible base in both views, so it hides more of the mover's near end, and the share of the mover it hides is measured on the renders). For every model: beta(15 cm) - beta(no wall) > 0, CI > 0, Holm across models, on movers whose contact is visible without the wall (>= 5 contact pixels in both views) and hidden by the 15 cm wall (none). Rationale: H6 hid 70 cm of a car and 35% of a crate; the lowest wall that still hides the contact in both views tests whether hiding the contact, rather than a large part of the body, raises the geometry share.
registered_hypotheses.rules: NOT TESTABLE below 8 movers or 5 base scenes; verdicts as for H5-H8 (SUPPORTED: interval > 0; CONTRADICTED: interval < 0; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise). The static-scene gate (Section 6.0) applies to both new testbeds.

exploratory_analyses.shape of the dose-response and of the sw: beta(70 cm) - beta(no wall), beta(70 cm) - beta(15 cm) and the share of the 70 cm effect reached at 15 cm, reported only where the 70 cm effect is clearly positive (a step points to the contact junction, a graded rise to the extent of the hidden lower body); beta by baseline for grounded and floating movers separately; M2 recall by baseline and by wall height.
exploratory_analyses.the static twin (Proposition 4, 3.11c, 6: on Argoverse 2 (all 64 logs) the camera height H above each vehicle's contact plane comes from its labelled box; the static twin of a vehicle then lies H (1 - e^x_geo) above that plane, below the road for a vehicle moving with the camera. Twin test: |twin height| above its 95th percentile over parked vehicles; epipolar test: |eps| above its 95th percentile over parked vehicles (5% false positives each). Recall of each test and of either, by motion regime and by s, with the detection curve the parked distribution implies. Correspondences come from labelled boxes: this measures what each test could see, not what a pipeline would.
exploratory_analyses.two channels: a cue model (6.11): per model, rho - rho_mono = w (x - rho_mono) with w = c_support d^2 / (d^2 + kappa^2) (d: translational parallax of the static-equivalent point in px; support: contact in view, contact hidden, unsupported), fitted by least squares on CONVOY-3D and E5 and compared by 10-fold cross-validation over scenes with the same model without parallax (kappa = 0) and without support (one c). Without refitting, the model then predicts the slope on BSW, WDR, CONVOY-REAL, E5-REAL and Argoverse 2; predicted and observed slopes are reported side by side. Also: binned rho against x on CONVOY-3D with the model's curve; MonST3R minus DUSt3R on the same movers (slope above 40 px of parallax, and the H6 contrast); the change of M2 recall against the change of beta_s between E5 conditions.
exploratory_analyses.CONVOY-REAL and parallax (6.11): correction of the v6.4 reading (D57): the CONVOY-REAL movers have far more parallax (median about 69 px) than the CONVOY-3D floating crates (median 13-17 px), so their higher slope may come from parallax, not from real images; the comparison is repeated within parallax bins and against the cue model.
exploratory_analyses.Bonn RGB-D Dynamic (3.12, 6.12): real balloons and boxes moved by people (four sequences), measured depth and motion-capture poses, A3 as for TUM. Moving regions as for TUM walking (Section 3.7); people masked by an off-the-shelf instance segmenter; per object: its regime (parallel threshold: the flow-noise floor of static patches, at least 1 px), x_geo from the flow correspondence after a per-pair scale check on static pixels, and the height of its lowest point above the floor. All six models are evaluated on the pairs; reported are the regime shares and the per-object geometry share g of parallel objects by kind (balloon, box, person) and by floor contact. Because x_geo is built from flow and sensor depth (D24), no slope is estimated; only per-object shares with |x - rho_mono| >= 0.3 enter.

why: The v6.4 run showed that ground support goes with the geometry share in every testbed, and that the rise of beta_s with parallax is specific to DUSt3R and MASt3R. Two readings remained open: that parallax rather than support drives part of the effect (the CONVOY-REAL movers have far more parallax than the CONVOY-3D floating crates), and that the contact effect needs a large occluder. The two designed experiments test these with registered predictions; the twin, the cue model and Bonn connect the result to geometry and to real objects without changing any verdict.
